البلاغة.def: The art of using language effectively and persuasively, focusing on the style, structure, and impact of words and sentences.

علم المعاني.def: The study of the meanings of words and sentences in the Arabic language, focusing on how context and structure affect interpretation.

علم البيان.def: The study of the expressive aspects of language, including metaphor, simile, and other figures of speech that enhance the clarity and beauty of communication.

علم البديع.def: The study of rhetorical devices and techniques that enhance the aesthetic and persuasive qualities of language, including alliteration, assonance, and other stylistic elements.

جملة الاسمية.def: A جملة اسمية (nominal sentence) is a sentence in Arabic that begins with a noun (إسم) or a pronoun (ضمير)
examples:
الْوَلَدُ مُجْتَهِدٌ
The boy is diligent

الْكِتَابُ جَدِيدٌ
The book is new

جملة الفعلية.def: A جملة فعلية (verbal sentence) is a sentence in Arabic that begins with a verb (فعل)

الفعل.def: The action word that sets the tense (past, present, or command)
examples:
كَتَبَ
He wrote

يَجْرِي
He runs

الفاعل.def: The doer of the action, which follows the verb and takes a nominative case (marfu')
examples:
سافرَ خالدٌ إلى مكة
Khalid travelled to Mecca

اقرأْ الكتابَ
Read the book

المفاعيل.def: refers to a noun that is affected by or involved in the action of a verb.

المفعول به.def: The receiver of the action, which is optional and takes an accusative case (mansub) if present
examples:
أكلَ الولدُ التفاحةَ
The boy ate the apple

قرأَتْ فاطمةُ قصةً
Fatima read a story

المفعول المطلق.def: A verbal noun derived from the verb itself, used to emphasize the action or show its type/count
examples:
ضَرَبْتُهُ ضَرْبًا
I hit him a hard blow

نطق المتكلّم كلاماً فصيحاً
The speaker uttered eloquent speech

المفعول فيه.en: Adverbial Object of TIme or Place
المفعول فيه.def: The ظرف (Zarf) or time/place indicator showing when or where the action happened
examplees:
جَلَسَ الطِّفْلُ أَمَامَ المُعَلِّمِ
The child sat in front of the teacher

ظرف زمان.def: These words tell us when an action happens
examples: الآن (Now)
غدًا (Tomorrow)
صباحًا (In the morning)

ظرف مكان.def: These words tell us where an action happens
examples: هنا (there)
تحت (below)

حال.def: These words describe how an action is performed
examples: بهدوء (Slowly)
سريعًا (Quickly)

المفعول لأجله.def: A noun explaining the reason or intention behind why the action was done
examples:
وَقَفْتُ إِجْلَالًا لِلْمُعَلِّمِ
I stood up out of respect for the teacher
يَجۡعَلُونَ   أَصَٰبِعَهُمۡ   فِيٓ   ءَاذَانِهِم   مِّنَ   ٱلصَّوَٰعِقِ   حَذَرَ   ٱلۡمَوۡتِۚ [2:19]

المفعول معه.def: A noun following a waw (Waw al-Maiyah) meaning "along with" or "alongside" indicating accompaniment
examples:
سِرْتُ وَالنِّيلَ
I walked alongside the Nile River

اسْتَيْقَظْتُ وَأَذَانَ الفَجْرِ
I wake up at the dawn right at the call of prayer

المبتدأ.def: The subject of a nominal sentence (جملة اسمية)
examples:
الماءُ باردٌ
The water is cold

الخبر.def: that can be judged as true or false; such as affirmative or negative

types.name: خبر مفرد
types.def: A single word that can be judged as true or false.
examples:
الجو جميل
(The weather is beautiful)

العلمُ نافعٌ
(Knowledge is beneficial)

types.name: خبر جملة
types.def: A sentence that can be judged as true or false
examples:
الجو جميل اليوم
(The weather is beautiful today)

الحَدِيقَةُ أَسْوَارُهَا جَمِيلَةٌ
(The garden's fences are beautiful)

types.name: خبر شبه جملة
types.def: consists of either a prepositional phrase (جار ومجرور) or an adverbial phrase (ظرف)
examples:
العصفور في القفصِ
(The bird is in the cage)

السفرُ غداً
(The travel is tomorrow)

الإنشاء.def: That cannot be judged as true or false such as a command or request

types.name: الإنشاء الطلبي
types.def:
A request that cannot be judged as true or false.
Examples include
  • النهي/الأمر (Command)
  • الاستفهام (Question)
  • التمني (Longing)
  • النداء (Cry)
examples:
أعطني الكتاب
(Give me the book)

types.name: الإنشاء غير الطلبي
types.def:
A non-request that cannot be judged as true or false.
Examples include
  • التعجب (Exclamation)
  • المدح والذم (Praise and Criticism)
  • القسم (Vow)
  • الرجاء (Hope)
examples:
ما أجمل هذا اليوم
(How beautiful this day is)

الفصل.def: Conjoining sentences with the conjunction 'و' (and) can affect the meaning and interpretation of the sentence
examples: فَلۡيَضۡحَكُواْ   قَلِيلٗا   وَلۡيَبۡكُواْ   كَثِيرٗا [9:82]

الوصل.def: Omitting the conjunction 'و' (and) can affect the meaning and interpretation of the sentence
examples: يُدَبِّرُ   ٱلۡأَمۡرَ   يُفَصِّلُ   ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ [13:2]

القصر.def: restricting or confining one thing to another to show exclusivity and a specific limit.
examples: وَمَا   مُحَمَّدٌ   إِلَّا   رَسُولٞ [3:144]
إِنَّمَا   يَخۡشَى   ٱللَّهَ   مِنۡ   عِبَادِهِ   ٱلۡعُلَمَٰٓؤُاْۗ [35:28]
إِيَّاكَ   نَعۡبُدُ   وَإِيَّاكَ   نَسۡتَعِينُ [1:5]

الشجاع يصدق لا يكذب
The brave person tells the truth, not lies

التشبيه.def: Simile or direct comparison using explicit sharing of traits
examples:
الرجل كالأسد في شجاعته
The man is like a lion in his bravery

الرجل أسد
The man is (as brave as) a lion

المجاز.def: Metaphor or figurative usage where a word is used outside its literal definition

types.name: المجاز اللغوي
types.def: A metaphor where the implied meaning is derived from the linguistic context and usage of words rather than direct comparison.
examples:
رأيت أسدًا يحارب في المعركة
I saw a lion (somone brave enough) fighting in the battlefield

types.name: المجاز العقلي
types.def: A metaphor where the implied meaning is derived from logical reasoning and understanding of concepts rather than direct comparison.
examples:
دَارَتْ بي الأيامُ
The days have turned against me (I have faced many hardships)

types.name: المجاز بالحذف
types.def: A metaphor where a word is used in a figurative sense by omitting its literal meaning, relying on the context to convey the intended message.
examples:
وَاسْأَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ
Ask the village (ask the people of the village)

الكناية.def: Metonymy or an expression pointing to a secondary implied meaning while keeping the literal sense open

types.name: كنايات العدد
types.def: A metonymy where a word is used to imply a specific quantity or number, while keeping the literal sense open.
examples:
كم كتاباً قرأت؟
How many books did you read? (The word 'كم' implies a specific number of books, while keeping the literal sense open)

اشتريتُ كذا كتاباً
I bought several books (The word 'كذا' implies a specific number of books, while keeping the literal sense open)

types.name: كنايات الحديث والقصص
types.def: A metonymy where a word is used to imply a specific speech or story, while keeping the literal sense open.
examples:
نَهَى عَنْ كَيْتَ وَكَيْتَ
He forbade (the story of) Kayt and Kayta (The word 'نَهَى' implies a specific story, while keeping the literal sense open)

ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى القَاضِي فَقُلْتُ لَهُ كَيْتَ وَكَيْتَ، فَقَالَ لِي ذَيْتَ وَذَيْتَ
I went to the judge and told him (the story of) Kayt and Kayta, and he said to me (the story of) Zayt and Zayta (The words 'كَيْتَ وَكَيْتَ' and 'ذَيْتَ وَذَيْتَ' imply specific stories, while keeping the literal sense open)

الاستعارة.def: Borrowed metaphor (a specialized type of majaz) where a root word is applied based on a hidden resemblance

types.name: لاستعارة التصريحية
types.def: A metaphor where the implied meaning is explicitly stated, making the figurative sense clear and direct.
examples:
رأيت بَحراً يُعطي الفقراء
I saw a sea (a generous person) giving to the poor

types.name: الاستعارة المكنية
types.def: A metaphor where the implied meaning is suggested or hinted at, requiring the reader to infer the figurative sense from the context.
examples:
طَارَ الرَّجلُ من فَرْحَتِهِ
The man flew with joy (The man was extremely happy)

الطباق.def: The use of contrasting words or ideas in close proximity to create a striking effect and emphasize differences.
examples: وَتَحۡسَبُهُمۡ أَيۡقَاظٗا وَهُمۡ رُقُودٞۚ [18:18]

العِلْمُ نُورٌ وَالْجَهْلُ ظَلَامٌ
Knowledge is light and ignorance is darkness

المقابلة.def: The placement of contrasting words or ideas in close proximity to highlight their differences and create a more impactful effect.
examples:
نَّكُمْ لَتَكْثُرُونَ عِنْدَ الْفَزَعِ، وَتَقِلُّونَ عِنْدَ الطَّمَعِ
You are abundant in times of fear, and scarce in times of greed

الخير والشر
Good and Evil

الجناس.def: The use of words that sound similar but have different meanings, creating a play on words and enhancing the aesthetic quality of language.
examples: وَيَوۡمَ   تَقُومُ   ٱلسَّاعَةُ [30:14

سَمَّيْتُهُ يَحْيَى لِيَحْيَا
I named him Yahya so that he may live

السجع.def: A form of prose that employs a rhythmic and rhyming structure, creating a musical and harmonious effect in the language.
examples:
فِيهَا سُرُرٞ مَّرۡفُوعَةٞ ١٣
وَأَكۡوَابٞ مَّوۡضُوعَةٞ ١٤ [88:13]

أَلَمۡ نَجۡعَل لَّهُۥ عَيۡنَيۡنِ ٨
وَلِسَانٗا وَشَفَتَيۡنِ ٩ [90:8]
